mcqs.question: Which statement correctly compares latitude with longitude?

options.A: Latitude lines run east‑west and measure north‑south position; longitude lines run north‑south and measure east‑west position.
options.B: Latitude lines run north‑south and measure east‑west position; longitude lines run east‑west and measure north‑south position.
options.C: Both latitude and longitude lines run east‑west and measure the same direction.
options.D: Latitude measures distance from the Prime Meridian, while longitude measures distance from the Equator.

mcqs.answer: Latitude lines run east‑west and measure north‑south position; longitude lines run north‑south and measure east‑west position.
mcqs.explanation: Latitude lines are parallel to the Equator and run east‑west; they tell how far north or south a place is from the Equator. Longitude lines run from pole to pole (north‑south) and tell how far east or west a place is from the Prime Meridian. Options B, C, and D mix up these definitions.

mcqs.question: In competitive geography exams, which description best defines longitude?

options.A: Imaginary lines that run parallel to the Equator and measure north‑south distance.
options.B: Imaginary lines that run from the North Pole to the South Pole and measure east‑west position relative to the Prime Meridian.
options.C: Lines that indicate the distance of a place from the Equator.
options.D: Lines that are only used to locate places on the Prime Meridian.

mcqs.answer: Imaginary lines that run from the North Pole to the South Pole and measure east‑west position relative to the Prime Meridian.
mcqs.explanation: Longitude lines, also called meridians, extend from pole to pole and indicate how far east or west a location is from the Prime Meridian (0° longitude). Option A describes latitude, while C and D are inaccurate.

mcqs.question: What is the Equator?

options.A: A line that runs from the North Pole to the South Pole.
options.B: The line that passes through Greenwich, England.
options.C: The imaginary line that circles the Earth equidistant from the poles, dividing it into Northern and Southern Hemispheres.
options.D: A line that marks the boundary between the Eastern and Western Hemispheres.

mcqs.answer: The imaginary line that circles the Earth equidistant from the poles, dividing it into Northern and Southern Hemispheres.
mcqs.explanation: The Equator is at 0° latitude, halfway between the North and South Poles, and separates the Earth into two hemispheres. Options A and D describe meridians, while B describes the Prime Meridian.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly explains the Prime Meridian?

options.A: It is the line that divides the Earth into the Northern and Southern Hemispheres.
options.B: It is the line that runs parallel to the Equator at 23.5° north.
options.C: It is the line that marks the International Date Line.
options.D: It is the zero‑degree longitude line that passes through Greenwich, England.

mcqs.answer: It is the zero‑degree longitude line that passes through Greenwich, England.
mcqs.explanation: The Prime Meridian is defined as 0° longitude and runs through Greenwich, serving as the reference for measuring east‑west positions. Options A, B, and C describe other geographic lines.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes how latitude and longitude are used together to locate a place?

options.A: Latitude gives the north‑south position, while longitude gives the east‑west position; together they pinpoint a location.
options.B: Latitude and longitude both give only north‑south positions, so they cannot locate a place alone.
options.C: Longitude alone is sufficient to locate any place on Earth because it measures distance from the Equator.
options.D: Latitude alone determines the exact location because it measures distance from the Prime Meridian.

mcqs.answer: Latitude gives the north‑south position, while longitude gives the east‑west position; together they pinpoint a location.
mcqs.explanation: A pair of coordinates (latitude, longitude) uniquely identifies a point on the Earth's surface. Options B, C, and D misunderstand the roles of latitude and longitude.

mcqs.learning_point: Understanding location through intersecting reference lines
mcqs.question: A place has the coordinates 23° N latitude and 77° E longitude. Which Indian city is closest to this location?
mcqs.explanation: Bhopal lies at approximately 23° N, 77° E, matching the given coordinates. Delhi (≈28.6° N, 77.2° E) is farther north, Mumbai is far south‑west, and Chennai is far south‑east.

mcqs.question: Which of the following cities is situated at a higher latitude (farther north) than the others?
mcqs.explanation: Oslo is at about 60° N, making it far north of Nairobi (≈1° S), Delhi (≈28° N), and Kolkata (≈22° N). Higher latitude means a location is closer to the North Pole.

mcqs.question: A ship sails eastward and crosses the Prime Meridian. Which statement about its longitude is true after crossing?

options.A: Its longitude changes from a western (negative) value to an eastern (positive) value.
options.B: Its latitude increases because it moves farther from the Equator.
options.C: Its time zone remains exactly the same because longitude does not affect time.
options.D: Its distance from the Equator decreases as it moves eastward.

mcqs.answer: Its longitude changes from a western (negative) value to an eastern (positive) value.
mcqs.explanation: Crossing the Prime Meridian (0° longitude) from west to east changes the sign of the longitude coordinate from negative (west) to positive (east). Latitude is unchanged by east‑west movement, time zones shift with longitude, and distance from the Equator depends on latitude, not longitude.
